subject: Re: POC Observability Plan and Success Criteria
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC Observability — follow-up & proposed success criteria

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the discovery call today — really appreciated the context you shared about FinTechX's payment reconciliation workload and the main risk areas you want visibility into. As promised, here is a concise recap and a proposed observability plan for the POC so we can align on success criteria and next steps.

TL;DR proposed POC scope (3 weeks):
- Run Redwood inference on a representative subset (10M tokens/day equivalent) of your reconciliation prompts.
- Provide an observability dashboard and traces for the calls in scope.
- Define success criteria for latency, token cost reduction (via batching/caching), and correctness/regression thresholds.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 350ms for single-turn reconciliation prompts during normal load.
2) Cost: measured per-token cost reduction >= 20% vs current baseline after enabling recommended batching and cache settings.
3) Accuracy/regressions: end-to-end outputs must match your golden set with <= 2% regression in core reconciliation metrics (false positive/false negative rate as defined in your eval doc).
4) Reliability: no more than 1% error rate (timeouts, 5xx) during the POC window.

Observability plan (what Redwood will deliver):
- Dashboards: pre-built Grafana dashboard (hosted) covering token/req throughput, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), error breakdown, model variant routing counts, and cost per thousand tokens.
- Tracing: distributed traces for request lifecycle with span for routing, model execution, and kv-cache hits/misses.
- Logs: structured request logs (redacted) exported to your S3 bucket (or SFTP) on a daily roll-up and available for ad-hoc download.
- Metrics to monitor: request_count, tokens_generated, latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), error_count_by_code, cache_hit_rate, average_batch_size, cost_per_token_usd.
- Alerting: suggested alert thresholds and ownership for latency spikes (> p95 threshold), error rate, and cost anomalies.

Next steps we suggest:
1) You confirm success criteria and whether we should adjust the latency/cost targets.
2) Agree on POC timeline (we proposed 3 weeks) and target start date.
3) Provide access details for logs delivery (S3 bucket + IAM role OR SFTP) and a sample of reconciliation prompts (anonymized).
4) We’ll schedule a kickoff with Engineering (Marcus) and Solutions (Marissa) on the operational plan and dashboard walkthrough.

I attached a checklist that outlines the observability artifacts we’ll deliver and what we need from your side.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through if helpful.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-poc-observability-checklist.xlsx
From: Emma Chen <emma@fintechx.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Mehta <rahul@fintechx.com>, Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@fintechx.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: POC Observability — follow-up & proposed success criteria

Jordan —

Thanks for the thorough recap, that looks like the right level of detail. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency target: 350ms p95 is acceptable as a stretch goal; for procurement we need a conservative target of p95 < 450ms. Can we show both?
- Cost reduction: 20% baseline is attractive. We’ll provide current token-cost baseline and a sample of anonymized prompt pairs.
- Accuracy: we will share a golden set (approx 500 records) and the reconciliation metrics we track.

Log delivery: we prefer S3 with an IAM role — I will send the bucket name and role ARNs to Lisa.
POC timeline: 3 weeks is fine; tentative start 2026-09-15 if that works for you.

Also looped in Lisa from procurement to start the minimal paperwork for a short-term contract for the POC.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Chen
Head of ML Ops | FinTechX

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Chen <emma@fintechx.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: POC Observability — follow-up & proposed success criteria

Marcus/Marissa —

Looping you both in after FinTechX confirmed the broad criteria and a proposed 3-week POC starting 2026-09-15. Action items for engineering & solutions:
- Marcus: can you confirm we can provide the hosted Grafana dashboard and tracing spans (sampling at 100% for POC) and an export job to S3 by Day 3 of the POC?
- Marissa: please own the customer-facing runbook and dashboard walkthrough; schedule a 60min kickoff with FinTechX.
- I'll handle contract/PO intake with Lisa (procurement) and coordinate the POC start date.

Key engineering notes: we should enable prefix caching for their reconciliation prompt shapes and configure automatic batching with max latency 50ms to try to hit the cost/latency tradeoff. See attached checklist for mapping of artifacts to dates.

Please reply with confirmations and any blockers.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Chen <emma@fintechx.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC Observability — follow-up & proposed success criteria

Thanks — confirming items from infra side:
- Grafana dashboard: we have a POC template ready. We will deploy a customer instance and populate it with the following panels by Day 2:
  * Request throughput (rps) and tokens per minute
  * Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
  * Error breakdown by code (4xx/5xx/timeout)
  * Cache hit rate and average batch size
  * Cost per token estimates (derived metric)
- Tracing: we can enable full traces for the POC (100% sampling) and provide trace links in the dashboard. Spans will include routing, model execution, and cache lookup outcome.
- Logs export: will deliver a daily gzipped JSONL export to the S3 bucket provided. We will redact PII and only include request metadata + anonymized input ids.
- Deliverables timeline:
  Day 0-1: infra prep & credentials exchange
  Day 2-3: dashboard provisioned + basic data flowing
  Day 4-7: run baseline workload and collect metrics
  Week 2: apply batching/cache tuning; measure cost delta
  Week 3: finalize evaluation, handover report and regression analysis

I attached the POC observability checklist and the proposed SLA draft for the POC window. No blockers from our side; we just need the S3 IAM role and the anonymized prompt sample.

— Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma/Lisa —

I’ll send calendar invites for the kickoff and a shared folder with the POC checklist and the HubSpot deal link. If anything slips on your side, flag it here and we’ll re-align.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
